VAPP-260 (Engine E0, epic VAPP-259, docs/spec/apps.md §13.1): THE CAPABILITY CATALOG AND THE ONE BROKER. A CAPABILITY is a native tool provider the HOST implements per platform (E5) and mounts on the Engine's in-process MCP Proxy hub (packages/emcp hub.json) under its `name` (a hub server name: `hubServerNameValid`, never a `reservedNames` entry, so no capability can shadow the package's own functions or the Engine's internals). It declares SCOPES (`scopes`): a scope id `<capability>.<scope>` (`scopePattern`) is what a package's capability manifest names (package format 5 `capabilities: [{id, why, origins?}]`) and what a grant is kept for; each scope lists its TOOLS and its CONSENT: `ask` = the Engine's consent sheet once, the answer persisted (consent.json); `picker` = the platform's own picker or sheet IS the consent, every call, so nothing persists and the call needs the app in the foreground; `hostOnly: true` = a scope of the host itself (eDE's `shell.edit`, editing its ede-ui documents), NEVER in a manifest (the validator refuses it) and never granted to an app. `origins: true` = the manifest entry must list `origins` (exact `https://host[:port]` origins) and a call's `url` must be on one. NAMES: an agent calls `<capability>__<tool>` (exposes.json's qualified name, server = capability); app UI calls the function `<capability>.<tool>` (it must be in the package's `functions` allowlist like any other function); BOTH parse to the same `{capability, tool}` (`parseCases`), anything else is `unknown`. THE BROKER (`decideCases`, `brokerDecide`) is ONE function for UI and agent calls: the FIRST of: `unknown` (no such capability or tool: the agent answer is MCP's unknown-tool error -32602, never a hint) · `denied/hostOnly` · `denied/notDeclared` (the manifest is the CEILING: no scope declared = no call, no sheet) · `unavailable` (this host does not provide the capability, e.g. `camera` on a desktop without one) · `denied/originNotDeclared` (an `origins` scope whose `url` argument is missing or off the list) · for `picker`: `denied/needsForeground` in the background, else `call` · for `ask`: the stored grant `granted` = `call`, `denied` = `denied/consentDenied`, undecided = `ask` in the foreground (the Engine shows the consent sheet; consent.json `consentAnswer` turns the answer into the call's verdict) and `denied/consentNeeded` in the background (never a sheet behind the user's back). An agent's tools/list (`listCases`, `agentToolList`) = every tool of a scope the manifest declares and the host provides, `hostOnly` excluded, sorted by qualified name; a denied scope stays listed (the call answers `consentDenied`, so the agent can tell the person). THE AUDIT (`auditCases`, `brokerAuditRow`): every call, refused ones included, writes ONE row in audit.json's shape to the host's sink: `appId` = the package id, `clientId` = `ui` for app UI or the run id for an agent, `tool` = the qualified name `<capability>__<tool>` for both, `status` = `denied` for every refusal and `unknown`/`unavailable`, else audit.json's status of the call's outcome (`ok`, `isError` -> failed, `invalidParams` -> invalid, `rpcError`/`unreachable`/`timeout` -> upstream), `error` = the refusal's reason (`unknownTool` for unknown, `unavailable`), null on ok and failed; `argsHash` = audit.json's hash of the arguments as received. No hub tool writes the package, the grants or the host config: a grant changes only in consent.json's `grantWrite`. CAPABILITIES V1 (VAPP-265, E5): the TOOLS (`tools`, sorted by name) lock every tool's name, its app-facing `inputSchema`/`outputSchema` (what app UI and agents see: an agent's tools/list lists them as `<capability>__<tool>` with the same description and schemas) and, for `runs: native`, the `nativeOutputSchema` a host's native provider answers; `runs: engine` = the Engine answers it itself (`print_pdf`, no native call; the capability must still be provided). A host's native capability implements EVERY native tool of its capability (one it cannot serve answers isError `unavailable`). THE BRIDGE (`bridgeCases`, `bridgeCall`) runs between the broker's `call` verdict and the native, the same for UI and agents: (1) VALIDATE the arguments (`validateCases`) against `inputSchema` with the subset `type` (one or a list; `integer` = an integral number) · `properties` · `required` · `additionalProperties: false` · `minimum`/`maximum` · `minLength`/`maxLength` (code points) · `minItems`/`maxItems` · `items` · `enum` · `format` (`date-time` = RFC 3339 with a zone; `token` = 1 to 64 of `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`; `uri` = an absolute http(s) URL; `base64` = the standard alphabet, padded) · `dependentRequired` · `anyOf`/`oneOf` of `required` sets; checked in that order per value: type, then for an object required (listed order), unknown keys (sorted), each property (schema order), dependentRequired (its key order; the path is the MISSING key's), anyOf, oneOf; for an array minItems, maxItems, then each item; the FIRST violation answers isError `invalidParams: <JSON pointer, / for the root> <keyword>` (audit outcome `invalidParams`) and the native never runs; a missing top-level property with a `default` gets it. (2) MAP to the native arguments: photos.*, files_open = the validated arguments; files_save = `{name, mimeType, data}`; share_send = the given `title`/`text`/`url` plus `file: {name, mimeType, data}` for a `fileId`; print_print = `{name, mimeType, data}` (`name` default `document.<pdf|png|jpg>`); notifications_post = `{id: "<app>/<id>", title, body|null, at|null, tap}` where `tap` = lifecycle.json's `{type: notificationTap, app, screen, params ({} default)}` or null without a `screen` (a `screen` must be one of the package's screens, else `invalidParams: /screen enum`) and an absent `id` is generated (`n-` + 32 lowercase hex), so a host hands the tap back as the instance's event and ids never collide across apps; notifications_cancel = `{id: "<app>/<id>"}`. A `fileId` resolves through the host's BlobStore (`v1.context` = the app and its screens; missing = isError `notFound: <fileId>`), `data` = its bytes in base64; `text` = its UTF-8 bytes. `mimeType` = the given one, else `v1.mimeByExtension` of the name's last `.ext` (case-insensitive), else sniffed from the bytes (`%PDF-` application/pdf, FF D8 FF image/jpeg, the PNG signature image/png, `GIF8` image/gif), else text/plain for a `text` and application/octet-stream; print_print takes only a sniffed PDF, PNG or JPEG (else isError `unsupportedFile`). (3) CHECK the native's result: an `isError` result passes through as is (audit `failed`); otherwise its `structuredContent` must match `nativeOutputSchema` (else isError `badResult: <pointer> <keyword>`, nothing stored). (4) STORE every object in it that carries `data` (depth first, in order): BlobStore `put(app, name, mimeType, bytes)` (ids in the cases: `blob-1`, `blob-2`, …), the object loses `data` and gains `size` (bytes) and `fileId`; notifications_post answers `{id}` (the app's own id). Every answer is an MCP call result `{content: [{type: text, text: <the structuredContent as JSON>}], structuredContent}`, errors `{content: [{type: text, text: <reason>}], isError: true}`. THE PDF (`pdf`, `pdfCases`, `print_pdf`): ONE layout both twins write byte for byte (sha256 + size locked): A4 (`pdf.page` points), margins 56, content width 483, the cursor y from 786 down to 56; fonts F1 Helvetica and F2 Helvetica-Bold (Type1, WinAnsiEncoding; `pdf.widths` = their widths per WinAnsi code in 1/1000 em, `pdf.winAnsi` = the code points 0x80-0x9F map to; ASCII 0x20-0x7E and 0xA0-0xFF are themselves; a tab is a space, other controls drop, anything else is `?`). A text's width at size s = sum(widths) × s / 1000, compared exactly (sum × s ≤ 483000). Lines: a paragraph per `
`, words split on runs of spaces, greedy, a word wider than the line broken at the longest fitting prefix (one character at least); an empty paragraph is one empty line. A line at size s and leading L: if the page has content and y − L < 56, a new page; then `BT /F<n> <s> Tf 56 <y − s> Td (<text>) Tj ET` (an empty line writes nothing) and y −= L. heading: y −= 12 first unless the page is empty, F2 18/24, then y −= 4. text: F1 11/15, then y −= 6. image (a JPEG: SOF0-SOF3 width, height and 1/3/4 components = DeviceGray/RGB/CMYK, DCTDecode as is; a PNG: 8-bit, colour type 0 or 2, not interlaced, its IDATs concatenated with FlateDecode + DecodeParms Predictor 15; anything else isError `unsupportedImage: <fileId>`, a missing file `notFound: <fileId>`): scale = min(483/w, 730/h, 1), if the page has content and y − h·scale < 56 a new page, `q <w·scale> 0 0 <h·scale> 56 <y − h·scale> cm /Im<k> Do Q`, y −= h·scale; its caption: y −= 4, F1 9/12 lines; then y −= 6. pageBreak: a new page unless the page is empty. The last page is dropped if it is empty and not the only one. Numbers print rounded to 2 decimals, shortest form (`12`, `12.5`). Text strings escape `(`, `)` and `\` and write bytes ≥ 0x80 as 3-digit octal. The file: `%PDF-1.4
%` E2 E3 CF D3 `
`; objects `<n> 0 obj
<body>
endobj
`: 1 the Catalog, 2 Pages (Kids, Count), 3 F1, 4 F2, 5 Info (`/Title <FEFF…>` UTF-16BE uppercase hex, `/Producer (Exponential Engine)`), then one XObject per image file in first-use order (`/Im1`…, a file used twice is one object), then per page its Page (MediaBox, `/Resources << /Font << /F1 3 0 R /F2 4 0 R >> /XObject << … >> >>`, the XObject dict only with the page's images in number order) and its content; a stream body is `<< … /Length <n> >>
stream
<data>
endstream` (content data = the page's operators joined by `
`); then `xref
0 <size>
0000000000 65535 f 
`, one `<10-digit offset> 00000 n 
` per object, `trailer
<< /Size <size> /Root 1 0 R /Info 5 0 R >>
startxref
<offset>
%%EOF
`. The file is stored as `name` (default the title with `/\:*?"<>|` and controls replaced by `-`, + `.pdf`), application/pdf; the answer `{file, pages}`.

tools.name: files_open
tools.description: Let the person pick files to open. `accept` = MIME types (`image/*`) or extensions (`.csv`). Answers the files, each stored as an app file; an empty list when they cancel.

tools.name: files_save
tools.description: Let the person save an app file (`fileId`) or a text (`text`) where they pick. `saved` = false when they cancel.

tools.name: notifications_cancel
tools.description: Withdraw a notification this app posted or scheduled.

tools.name: notifications_post
tools.description: Post a notification now, or at `at` (an ISO time). A tap opens `screen` with `params`. Posting an `id` again replaces it.

tools.name: photos_get
tools.description: Read one photo of the library by its id (from list or pick), stored as an app file.

tools.name: photos_list
tools.description: The library's photos, newest first, without their bytes. Pass the answered cursor for the next page; null = the end.

tools.name: photos_pick
tools.description: Let the person pick photos in the platform's photo picker. Answers the picked photos, each stored as an app file; an empty list when they cancel.

tools.name: print_pdf
tools.description: Lay out a document (headings, text, app images, page breaks) as an A4 PDF, stored as an app file. No dialog: save, share or print the file next.

tools.name: print_print
tools.description: Open the platform's print dialog for an app file (a PDF, PNG or JPEG). `printed` = false when they cancel.

tools.name: share_send
tools.description: Open the platform's share sheet with a text, a link and/or an app file. `shared` = false when they dismiss it (true where the platform cannot tell).

Three days at the lake.

The last evening, (quiet) \ calm.
